discovery_articles.title: Egri Minaret in Eger, Hungary
discovery_articles.snippet: The northernmost surviving minaret in mainland Europe is a very claustrophobic reminder of the 16th- and 17th-century Ottoman occupation of Hungary. Ascend the 98 very cosy steps for a view over the surrounding town. The 40-metre-high tower, that now stands alone on the corner of an old town street in Eger, was once part of a mosque established by the Ottomans during their rule of the city in the early 1600s.
discovery_articles.ferns_note: The mosque is long gone, but this slender Ottoman minaret has been quietly outlasting empires on a sleepy Hungarian street corner for four centuries. Climb its 98 spiral steps and you emerge, breathless, over a city that has almost entirely forgotten the world this tower was built for.

featured_read.title: How to Be a Good Explorer on the Lifelong Expedition to Yourself
featured_read.snippet: Life is an ongoing expedition into the brambled tendrilled wilderness of ourselves, continually stymied by all we mistake for a final destination — success, superhuman strength, the love of another. Along the way, we keep confusing experiment and exploration. An experiment proves or disproves an existing theory; its payoff is data, fixed and binary.
featured_read.blurb: This essay draws a quiet but consequential distinction between experimenting on yourself and truly exploring yourself — one demands an answer, the other asks you to stay curious a little longer. Set aside the half-hour and let it reframe every wrong turn you've ever called a failure.

news.title: Thai Cucumber Salad
news.snippet: Thai cuisine is known (and loved) for its iconic, piercing spice. I was introduced to spicy foods from the time that I was a baby, and to cool down in between bites, I wouldn’t reach for milk or water; instead, I took in a forkful of crisp cucumber salad. Its cool, refreshing crunch was the perfect contrast to every spicy bite and is something that I often keep a bowl of in the fridge to eat as a side or snack.
news.blurb: A crunchy, cooling counterpoint to Thai heat — this one's a tasty reminder that the unsung heroes of a spicy spread are often the simplest ones.

news.title: How to cook the perfect apricot galette – recipe | Felicity Cloake's how to make the perfect …
news.snippet: A free-form fruit tart that’s easy to throw together with whatever seasonal fruit you have to hand The galette takes its name from the pebble it’s said to resemble – as Elizabeth David observes, it takes many forms, all of them round and flat. For me the word conjures the buckwheat pancakes of Brittany while French friends, in a quick straw poll, tend to think first of the frangipane-stuffed puff pastry galette de rois served at Epiphany, with one vote for a buttery Breton biscuit. Ask the English-language internet, however, and you’ll be served what is more commonly known as a tart(e), more specifically a charmingly rustic, free-form version which doesn’t require a tin.
news.blurb: Felicity Cloake does the obsessive testing so you don't have to, and this deep dive into the rustic, pebble-named galette is a gloriously timely read while stone fruits are having their moment.
